study_identification_part.si4_title: Understanding the heterogeneity of dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug naïve depression using normative models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To combine the dynamic features of fMRI data and normative modeling to quantitative and individualized metrics for delineating the biological heterogeneity of first-episode drug-naïve major depressive disorders (FEDN-MDD).

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The supplementary material provides a detailed description of the preprocessing pipeline.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: First, the initial 10 volumes were discarded, and then the slice-timing correction was performed. Second, the images were realigned using a six-parameter (rigid body) linear transformation. After realignment, individual T1-weighted images were co-registered to the mean functional image using a 6 degrees-of-freedom linear transformation without re-sampling and then segmented. Finally, transformations from individual native space to MNI space were computed. A linear trend was included as a regressor and temporal bandpass filtering (0.01-0.1Hz) was performed on the all-time series.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Statistical comparisons of z scores yielding from network-dynamic characteristics were conducted to explore the differences between groups. The pseudo two-sample t-test at a 5 % significance level (permutation tests, n = 10,000) was used to quantify the statistical significance of group differences.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study mapped the biological heterogeneity of FEDN-MDD using normative modeling of dynamic functional connectivity, finding significant deviations in DMN, left ECN, and limbic circuits, particularly in male patients.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found that 42.3% of patients and 38.5% of controls showed extreme deviations in at least one brain network. Weight variability was significantly increased in patients with FEDN-MDD, especially in males. Patients showed increased network-dynamic deviance in the default mode network (DMN), left-executive control network (ECN), and limbic network. 4.74% of patients showed a deviation of dynamic functional connectivity in above 100 connectivities, compared to 3.35% of controls.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Normative modeling might provide an excellent tool for understanding the heterogeneity of psychiatric disorders, and can be used as complementary to classical case-control comparisons.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The normative model was based on cross-sectional data and should be validated in a longitudinal cohort. No associations were found between the severity of symptoms and the percentage of deviation from the normative model. The choice of window length may have a potential influence on the results.
